newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer on cash buying for book closings.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer on cash buying for book closings.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed firmer on Wednesday after recouping earlier losses on the back of investors' consistent demand for cash bonds.
Scattered buying came in after midday with operators aiming to increase JGB holdings at their book closings, traders said.

Today is the last day of cash JGBs for delivery within the current fiscal year. Earlier in the morning, life insurers sold long-term cash bonds in large lots after their sales resulted in the market's late nosedive on Tuesday.
The key June contract ended up 0.16 at 126.11.
The June's session high was at 126.20 when last-minute short-covering emerged from dealers, which was related to benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB options trading, traders said.
The June earlier fell to as low as 125.60.
"It was natural that a correction started after a one-week rally that had a price rise of nearly two yen," said a dealer at a Big-Four brokerage.
The June contract had risen for five straight days until Monday when it set a record high for any benchmark contract of 126.88.

But it fell sharply on Tuesday on news that the Finance Ministry would announce details of measures to improve land liquidity on March 31 and a senior Bank of Japan official's comments implying that the recent surge in JGBs had been overdone, traders said.
"The market fell this morning on life insurers' selling in long-term cash bonds and continued stop-loss selling from dealers who had bought above 126.50," a city bank dealer said.
"But life insurers were said to be among those who bought the 190th-193rd JGBs this afternoon in order not to reduce their bond holdings for the book closings," he said.

The yield of key 182nd 10-year bond stood at 2.250 percent at 0730 GMT, up 0.035 from Tuesday finish. The yield briefly rose as high as 2.315 percent, compared with a record low yield for any cash benchmark of 2.185 percent set on Monday.
Traders said aggressive bids on the payment side at the shorter-end of the yield curve in the interest rate swap (IRS) market were also responsible for the weakness in the morning.

"Profit-taking hit the short- to medium-term JGBs harder than the long-end of the yield curve because the yields of these bonds had been low for too long," said a senior dealer at another Big Four brokerage house.

Traders said the Japanese government's plan to reduce the state deficit to three percent or less of annual gross domestic product (GDP) by 2003 would be positive for the JGB market in the long run, but did not have an immediate impact.
The plan was announced by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Tuesday night.
A 10-year JGB auction expected next week is a focus, traders said. Investors may show a strong appetite for the new bond even if the coupon rate is set at 2.4 or 2.5 percent.
Japan's financial markets are closed on Thursday for a holiday. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
